newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian dlr trims losses, but troubles remain.
newsitem.headline: Australian dlr trims losses, but troubles remain.

text.p: The Australian dollar recouped a little of its offshore losses through a thin morning's trade in what was largely a technical reaction to an oversold position rather than any improvement in underlying sentiment.

Traders said volumes had dropped away sharply compared to Tuesday's brisk two-way tussle and sell orders in particular looked to have been filled for the moment. The scale and speed of the currency's retreat from Friday's US$0.7895 peak also argued for a bounce, perhaps to US$0.7760 or so.
But few could envisage a sustained recovery given the steady erosion of the currency's yield advantage over the U.S. dollar.
By 12.15 pm (0215 GMT) the dollar was digging in at US$0.7735/40 having edged up from an offshore low of US$0.7723, but was still well short of Tuesday's late US$0.7760/65.

Traders said immediate support was put at US$0.7720 and US$0.7705 while resistance had already been met around US$0.7745 this morning and the currency needed to recover US$0.7785 to counter the bearish trend.

The situation was much the same on the crosses where the currency steadied somewhat after the week's slide but too close to its lows for comfort. On the yen it was at 97.62/72 from a trough of 97.35 and a finish here Tuesday of 97.91/01.
In trade weighted terms it was off at 60.1 from a previous 60.3 close and a 60.8 finish Friday.

There were no official economic data out today, and little at all until the Q1 consumer price index next Wednesday, but Westpac will be releasing its April consumer sentiment index at 2.30 pm (0430 GMT).

This had bounced by 4.9 percent in March after diving 7.9 percent in February in a seesaw pattern which has characterised the survey since November last year and has made it hard to draw conclusions from monthly movements.
